title: Public Transport Fare Adjustment in Fare Review Exercise 2022
what_it_is: Public Transport Fare Adjustment in Fare Review Exercise 2022

sections.label: Fare adjustment carry-over and subsidies
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the carried-over 10.6% fare adjustment is on top of future maximums, when it takes effect, and whether cost of living is considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport given that 10.6% of the maximum allowable public transport fare adjustment quantum in the Fare Review Exercise (FRE) 2022 will be carried over to future exercises (a) whether this will be on top of the maximum allowable fare adjustment quantum for future FREs; (b) when is the earliest time it will be effected; and (c) whether cost of living concerns will be considered in deciding whether this quantum will be effected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport with regard to the additional Government subsidy of about $200 million in 2023 to support the public transport system (a) what is the amount of subsidy granted to (i) each public transport operator and (ii) households, respectively; and (b) whether the subsidies granted are in addition to or negates the need to implement the 10.6 percentage point fare increase for consumers that is carried over to future fare review exercises.

sections.label: Fare Review Exercise 2022 outcome
sections.summary: The fare formula set a 13.5% maximum, PTC implemented 2.9%, 10.6% is carried over, and Government provides about $200 million in subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In this year's FRE, the fare formula output set the maximum allowable fare adjustment at 13.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: PTC decided to implement a lower increase of 2.9% after considering the economic and social impact on commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The remaining 10.6% will be carried over to future FREs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Government will provide additional subsidies of about $200 million in the coming year to make up for the shortfall.

sections.label: Bus contracts and performance requirements
sections.summary: Bus contracts spell out performance requirements and operators are held closely to delivering key performance indicators.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: What we try to do is – because, specifically, the Member's point is on buses – bus contracts spell out clearly the performance requirements and we hold the public transport operators (PTOs) who are awarded the contracts closely to the delivery of those key performance indicators (KPIs).

sections.label: Rising costs and fare formula review
sections.summary: Costs have been rising while fares have not been near that rate, and a fare formula review exercise is underway.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I have pointed out, that is precisely the issue because our costs have been rising and our fares have not been anyway near that rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: There is a fare formula review exercise that is underway.

sections.label: Government funding for public transport
sections.summary: The Government has put in $2 billion and another $200 million for next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Well, the Government has stepped up and has clearly put in a significant amount – $2 billion, and another $200 million for next year.

sections.label: Allocation for public transport vouchers
sections.summary: This year and the previous exercise had a significant allocation for PTVs up to the 30th percentile of income-earning households.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As Members would have noticed, this year and, also in the previous exercise, there has been a very significant allocation for PTVs – up to the 30th percentile of income-earning households.
